title: A Archive for the Terminal
premise: Ines Delacroix smuggles stolen memories in sealed neural drives through the contested orbits of Halcyon Station, keeping her head down and her past erased. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream—a dying voice broadcasting from a decommissioned relay at the edge of dead space—Ines recognizes the signal as the archived consciousness of the colonists the corporation 'evacuated' five years ago, a purge she unknowingly helped erase. Hunted by corporate enforcers who need the evidence destroyed, Ines and a ragged crew of memory-runners must carry the archive to an open broadcast relay, choosing between their own survival and justice for the dead. The book ends with the truth transmitted to every colony in the system, Ines surrendering herself to buy the broadcast time, and the children's dream finally falling silent—not as loss, but as release.
about_author: Cyrus Thornbury is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for deep-space freight contracts before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable internet and strong opinions about vacuum-rated coffee.

chapters.title: Contraband Heartbeats
chapters.summary: POV: Ines. A routine smuggling run past orbital customs nearly turns fatal when a customs officer scans too close to a sealed drive of stolen memories. Ines escapes but realizes someone flagged her specifically. The emotional beat is wary competence masking loneliness—five years invisible, and now someone is looking.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Alike
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas, a nine-year-old dockworker's son, wakes screaming from a dream of drowning in starlight—then finds forty other children dreamed it too. His mother dismisses it; his grandmother goes pale and burns an old photograph. The beat is creeping dread: something buried on Halcyon is surfacing through its youngest.

chapters.title: Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: POV: Ines. Tracing the children's dream to its source, Ines discovers a repeating signal from Relay Kestrel, abandoned at the edge of dead space. The waveform matches memory-drive architecture—the dream is a compressed consciousness, leaking. Beat: horrified recognition, because she recognizes the encoding. She's carried this format before.

chapters.title: What the Corporation Evacuated
chapters.summary: POV: Mara Voss, corporate compliance director. Flashback chapters interleave with present-day orders to scrub all records of the 'Kestrel Resettlement' five years ago. Mara begins to grasp what was actually purged—and that Ines Delacroix's old shipping manifests are the thread that unravels everything. Beat: complicity curdling into fear.

chapters.title: A Crew of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Ines. Ines recruits her old smuggling network: Dez the forger, Okonkwo the retired pilot, and Sefa, whose sister was 'evacuated.' Each has a reason to stay hidden; each chooses to move anyway. Beat: reluctant belonging—the found family Ines refused to admit she needed, assembled under threat.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: POV: Okonkwo. The run to Relay Kestrel crosses dead space where no rescue exists. Enforcer ships shadow them; a micrometeorite strike cripples life support, forcing a brutal rationing choice. Beat: the price of survival made literal—who breathes, who waits, and what Ines is willing to spend to keep going.

chapters.title: Voices in the Drive
chapters.summary: POV: Ines. Sheltering in Kestrel's derelict ring, Ines plays the archive and meets them: three thousand stored minds, including the woman whose memories she once smuggled without knowing. They ask not for rescue but for witness. Beat: grief transformed into purpose—the dead are not cargo; they are plaintiffs.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Downward
chapters.summary: POV: Mara Voss. Corporate enforcers seize Halcyon Station, interrogating the children's families to find the smugglers. Mara, ordered to falsify the final report, instead leaks the manifests to Ines's crew—an act that will end her career or her life. Beat: justice outside the law, chosen from inside it.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Ines. At the relay's transmitter, enforcers close in. The archive needs eleven minutes to propagate system-wide; Ines stays at the console while her crew escapes, feeding herself into the uplink buffer to hold the channel open. Beat: climax and sacrifice—visibility at last, at the ultimate cost.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas, one year later. Every colony heard the names. Trials proceed; the children no longer dream the dream, but Tomas keeps one fragment—Ines's voice, thanking him for listening. Her crew rebuilds the smuggling routes into something lawful. Beat: bittersweet resolution—belonging won, survival redefined, justice begun.
